'''Lisa Jayne Jardine-Wright''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|size=100%|OBE}} (born 1976) is an English physicist and educator at the [[University of Cambridge]]. She is the director of [[Isaac Physics]], a [[Department for Education]] and the [[Peter Ogden (businessman)|Ogden Trust]] supported [[Open learning|open platform]] for active learning, which supports school students learning [[physics]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Prof Lisa Jardine-Wright, OBE|work=People Directory |url=https://www.phy.cam.ac.uk/profile/prof-lisa-jardine-wright/ |access-date=2025-11-15 |language=EN|publisher=University of Cambridge, Cavendish Laboratory, Department of Physics}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Professor Lisa Jardine-Wright |url=https://www.chu.cam.ac.uk/fellows/prof-lisa-jardine-wright/ |access-date=2025-11-15 |website=Churchill College |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Professor Lisa Jardine-Wright OBE |url=https://www.mollerinstitute.com/team/professor-lisa-jardine-wright/ |access-date=2025-11-15 |website=Møller Institute |language=en-GB}}</ref>

== Education and early career ==
Jardine-Wright attended a [[State-funded schools (England)|state-funded school]]{{which|date=October 2026}} in the [[North West England|North West of England]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.timeshighereducation.com/news/blue-sky-thinking-that-led-to-an-astronomical-ambition/310974.article|title=Blue-sky thinking that led to an astronomical ambition|date=2007-11-02|website=Times Higher Education (THE)|language=en|access-date=2019-07-03}}</ref> She studied physics at the [[University of Cambridge]]. She earned her master's degree at [[Trinity College, Cambridge]], before studying towards a doctorate with [[George Efstathiou]]. Jardine-Wright worked on simulating the cosmological formation of [[Spiral galaxy|spiral galaxies]] at the [[Institute of Astronomy, Cambridge]]. During her PhD she became interested in outreach and public engagement, and organised a series of open days and public lectures.<ref name=":0" /> She worked as a postdoctoral researcher on the formation of galaxies.<ref name=":0" /> During her postdoc, Jardine-Wright partnered with the Cambridge Astronomy Association to lead a series of stargazing evenings.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cambridgenetwork.co.uk/news/starry-starry-nights|title=Starry starry nights {{!}} Cambridge Network|website=www.cambridgenetwork.co.uk|access-date=2019-07-03}}</ref>

== Career ==
Jardine-Wright has worked in [[science communication]] and outreach. She was a [[British Science Association]] media fellow at the ''[[Financial Times]]'', and started to write for the ''[[Times Higher Education]]'' as well as for the journal [[Science (journal)|''Science'']].  She has also acted as a consultant for ''[[BBC News Magazine]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.uos.ac.uk/events/what-so-special-about-special-relativity-can-we-use-it-stay-younger-longer|title=What is so special about special relativity: Can we use it to stay younger for longer?|last=Holliday|first=Katie|date=2017-09-13|website=University of Suffolk|language=en|access-date=2019-07-03}}</ref> During her postdoctoral research she also worked as the astronomy consultant for the [[Royal Observatory, Greenwich]] for the redesign of their astronomy galleries and planetarium (opened in 2007).  Jardine-Wright is the educational outreach officer at the [[University of Cambridge]], where she runs several programmes, including Physics at Work and the Senior Physics Challenge.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.iop.org/careers/workinglife/articles/page_54871.html|title=Making outreach work|website=www.iop.org|access-date=2019-07-03}}</ref> She is a director of studies and undergraduate student tutor at [[Churchill College, Cambridge]] and served as acting senior tutor of the college during the spring and summer of the [[COVID-19 pandemic|pandemic year]] 2020. She has investigated the performance of undergraduate students at the [[University of Cambridge]], and the impact of gender and socioeconomic background.<ref name="Gibson et al 2015">{{cite journal |last1=Gibson |first1=Valerie |last2=Jardine-Wright |first2=Lisa |last3=Bateman |first3=Elizabeth |title=An investigation into the impact of question structure on the performance of first year physics undergraduate students at the University of Cambridge |journal=European Journal of Physics |date=1 July 2015 |volume=36 |issue=4 |article-number=045014 |doi=10.1088/0143-0807/36/4/045014 |bibcode=2015EJPh...36d5014G |s2cid=53466707 |doi-access=free |url=https://www.repository.cam.ac.uk/bitstreams/e3ffe108-0883-47b2-8128-2bdf64951ce6/download }}</ref> Despite all students being at the same academic level on entry to Cambridge, Jardine-Wright showed that women perform better with scaffolded as opposed to open questions.<ref name="Gibson et al 2015"/>

===Isaac Physics===
Since founding Isaac Physics<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://isaacphysics.org/|title=Isaac Physics|website=Isaac Physics}}</ref> in 2014, Jardine-Wright has acted as Director and co-director.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ice.cam.ac.uk/about-us/staff-profiles/tutor/dr-lisa-jardine-wright|title=Dr Lisa Jardine-Wright|last=Anonymous|date=2015-12-03|website=www.ice.cam.ac.uk|language=en|access-date=2019-07-03}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sec-ed.co.uk/news/physics-website-throws-down-a-level-gauntlet|title=Physics website throws down A level gauntlet|website=www.sec-ed.co.uk|access-date=2019-07-03}}</ref> Isaac Physics is an online collection of physics questions from the archive of the [[Cambridge Assessment International Education|Cambridge Assessment]] that looks to support school students studying [[physics]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cambridgeassessment.org.uk/news/how-questions-from-the-past-are-creating-the-physicists-of-tomorrow/|title=How questions from the past are creating the physicists of tomorrow|website=www.cambridgeassessment.org.uk|access-date=2019-07-03}}</ref> It originally began under the name of the Rutherford Schools Physics Partnership. Isaac Physics helps physics students prepare for the transition from school to university.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.librarianintraining.com/2016/04/|title=Librarian in Training|language=en-GB|access-date=2019-07-03}}</ref> Jardine-Wright is the author of an educational books for Isaac Physics.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://isaacbooks.org/authors.php|title=Isaac Physics Books|website=isaacbooks.org|access-date=2019-07-03}}</ref> From 2013, the project has been supported by the [[Department for Education]] with additional support from [[The Ogden Trust]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ogdentrust.com/|title=Promoting the teaching and learning of physics|first=The Ogden|last=Trust|date=February 23, 2021|website=The Ogden Trust}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/curriculum-fund-programme-pilots-list-of-lead-schools/curriculum-fund-programme-pilots-list-of-lead-schools-and-related-information|title=Curriculum fund programme pilots: list of lead schools and related information|website=GOV.UK|language=en|access-date=2019-07-03}}</ref> Isaac also supports students studying A-Level chemistry.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://isaacphysics.org/%7B%7BrelativeCanonicalUrl%7D%7D|title=Isaac Physics|website=Isaac Physics|language=en|access-date=2019-07-03}}</ref>

==Honours and awards==
Jardine-Wright was appointed [[Officer of the Order of the British Empire]] (OBE) in the [[2022 Birthday Honours]] for services to education.<ref>{{London Gazette|issue=63714|supp=y|page=B16|date=1 June 2022}}</ref>

* 2012 [[Institute of Physics]] [[Phillips Award]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.iop.org/about/awards/phillips/medallists/page_59232.html|title=Phillips Award recipients|website=www.iop.org|access-date=2019-07-03}}</ref>
* 2015 [[Times Higher Education]] Outstanding Digital Innovation (shortlisted)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.staff.admin.cam.ac.uk/general-news/isaac-physics-project-makes-awards-shortlist|title=Isaac Physics project makes awards shortlist|last=Davison|first=Tim|date=2015-09-18|website=For staff|language=en|access-date=2019-07-03}}</ref>
* 2017 [[University of Cambridge]] Pilkington Prize<ref>{{Citation|last=Cambridge University|title=Dr Lisa Jardine-Wright - Department of Physics|date=2017-06-30|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kDJyzmtwjrs|access-date=2019-07-03}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.chu.cam.ac.uk/news/2017/jun/22/lisa-jardine-wright-wins-pilkington-prize-2017/|title=Churchill Fellow, Dr Lisa Jardine-Wright wins University Pilkington Prize for excellence in teaching – Churchill College|website=www.chu.cam.ac.uk|date=22 June 2017 |access-date=2019-07-03}}</ref>
* 2019 [[Institute of Physics]] [[Lawrence Bragg Medal and Prize]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://beta.iop.org/2019-lawrence-bragg-medal-and-prize|title=2019 Lawrence Bragg Medal and Prize|website=2019 Lawrence Bragg Medal and Prize {{!}} Institute of Physics|language=en|access-date=2019-07-03}}</ref>
